clue.text: Clydeside Moll?

parts.note: read as the gangster's moll at the side of Clyde Barrow, whose first name is also the Scots word for pretty

explanation.surface: A gangster's girlfriend from the shipyards along Glasgow's river.
explanation.walkthrough: Clydeside suggests Glasgow, but it means 'beside Clyde': Clyde Barrow's partner in the 1930s American crime duo, whose name is also Scots for pretty.
explanation.definitionFit: Parker was the female half of the outlaw pair, a gangster's moll riding alongside Clyde.

clue.text: Retire oversea to an isolated place

definitions.meaning: on the water, rowers back the oars to retreat
a quiet place cut off from events, like a still bit of river

explanation.surface: Move abroad to somewhere remote.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oversea' suggests emigrating; on water, to retire is to row backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Rowing backwards to retreat is the verb; a stagnant pool off the main stream gives the sense of a remote spot.

clue.text: Vengeance seems in fashion

indicators.note: to fashion is to shape, so these letters are shaped anew

explanation.surface: Revenge appears to be stylish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in fashion' reads as stylish, but 'fashion' scrambles SEEMS and IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Retribution personified as the Greek goddess of revenge.

clue.text: Assured for what is bound to happen

definitions.meaning: certain, sure to come
the unavoidable, as in 'accept the ...'

explanation.surface: Confident about a coming event.
explanation.definitionFit: Something certain cannot be avoided; the unavoidable is what must come about.

clue.text: Not an "in" novelist

definitions.meaning: in cricket the side not batting, so not 'in', is out in the field
Henry, author of Tom Jones

explanation.surface: A writer who is not fashionable.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket one side is 'in' (batting) and the other is out in the field; Henry Fielding wrote Tom Jones.
explanation.definitionFit: The cricket side that is not batting spends its innings chasing the ball; Henry was an eighteenth-century writer of comic fiction.

clue.text: Confused political situation perhaps mob girl at No 10?

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters might be one possible arrangement of others

parts.note: number 10 written as the letters I and O

explanation.surface: A gangster's girlfriend at Downing Street, a political scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: No 10 suggests Downing Street, but the 10 is the letters IO; 'perhaps' scrambles them with MOB GIRL.
explanation.definitionFit: An entangled, embarrassing state of affairs, as in a diplomatic tangle.

clue.text: Jack can do this, says Philip

definitions.meaning: a car jack raises a vehicle
the name spoken sounds like fillip, a boost

explanation.surface: Jack is able to do it, according to Philip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Philip' is not a person; said out loud it is 'fillip', a boost.
explanation.definitionFit: A jack raises cars; a fillip is a boost or uplift.

clue.text: Choice language of The Mousetrap

parts.note: in Hamlet the play-within-a-play is The Mousetrap, whose story Hamlet says is written in very choice tongue of Italy

explanation.surface: A preferred tongue for Agatha Christie's long-running play.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mousetrap suggests Agatha Christie's play, but it is Hamlet's play within the play, whose source, he says, is 'written in very choice Italian'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamlet describes the source tale of his play as written in fine prose from Italy.

clue.text: Theatre-in-the-round

parts.note: read as Shakespeare's round playhouse on the Thames, and as a sphere

explanation.surface: A stage with the audience on every side.
explanation.walkthrough: Shakespeare's playhouse in Southwark was a round building, and its name means a sphere.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's wooden O was a circular playhouse whose name also means a sphere.

clue.text: Guns raised to sight animal

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: gats are guns in gangster slang

explanation.surface: A hunter lifts a rifle to aim at a beast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns GATS upwards in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A male deer is an animal.

clue.text: Animadversion that is indeed continental

definitions.meaning: a critical remark or observation
the French exclamation meaning 'what!' or 'indeed!', a word from across the Channel

explanation.surface: A critical remark that really is European.
explanation.walkthrough: In French the same word is an exclamation of surprise, roughly 'what!' or 'indeed!', hence continental.
explanation.definitionFit: An animadversion is a critical remark; the French use the same word as an exclamation of surprise.

clue.text: Member of neat family in American city

definitions.meaning: neat is an old word for cattle, and this beast belongs to the cattle family
a city in New York State on Lake Erie

explanation.surface: A relative from a tidy family living in a US city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neat' looks like tidy, but it is the old word for cattle (as in neatsfoot oil).
explanation.definitionFit: A large wild ox is a bovine, one of the cattle family; the name is also a city on Lake Erie.

clue.text: Nothing was misrepresented by this young feller

indicators.note: misrepresented means the letters of the two words are put into a false new arrangement

explanation.surface: A boy who chopped things down never told a lie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misrepresented' scrambles NOTHING and WAS. The legend has young George chop down a cherry tree and admit it, unable to lie: a young feller of trees who misrepresented nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: The future first US president, in the cherry-tree legend, was a boy who felled a tree.

clue.text: Forfeit sterling

definitions.meaning: a penalty paid in money
excellent, of high quality, like sterling silver

explanation.surface: Losing British currency.
explanation.definitionFit: A forfeit is a penalty, like a money charge for an offence; sterling means excellent or of good quality.

clue.text: People with career going soft here?

parts.note: a race is a people
a career is a course through life

explanation.surface: People whose careers are getting easier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going' is the state of the turf in horse racing; soft going is wet ground.
explanation.definitionFit: The ground condition, called the going, is reported at a horse-racing track.

clue.text: One whose final charge is legal?

definitions.text: One whose final charge is legal?

parts.words: One whose final charge is legal?
parts.note: read as a person whose last instructions, a valid will, are lawful at death

explanation.surface: Someone whose last accusation stands up in court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Final charge' is not an accusation but the last instructions of a will; to die having made a valid one is to die this way.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes a person who dies leaving a valid will, their last instructions having legal force.

clue.text: Fan, former tower of strength

parts.note: ex means former
a tractor is a powerful machine that tows

explanation.surface: An admirer who used to be a reliable support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fan' suggests an admirer, but it is a ventilating fan; 'tower' means one that tows.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitchen ventilator that draws out air is a kind of fan.

clue.text: Opsimath is late one to be a money-winner

definitions.text: Opsimath is late one to be a money-winner

parts.words: Opsimath is late one to be a money-winner
parts.note: an opsimath is a late student, and a money-winner is an earner

explanation.surface: Someone who studies late in life is a late developer as a breadwinner.
explanation.walkthrough: An opsimath is someone who begins to study late in life. A money-winner is an EARNER; put L (the learner-driver plate) in front and the student appears.
explanation.definitionFit: An opsimath is a person who takes up study late in life, a late student.

clue.text: Sorry about confined worker

parts.note: re means about or concerning
pent means shut in
an ant is a worker in the insect colony

explanation.surface: Regretful about an imprisoned labourer.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling regret for wrongdoing, contrite.

clue.text: Telephone rent is an overhead item

parts.note: to telephone someone is to ring them
to rent out a property is to let it

explanation.surface: A phone bill counts as one of the business overheads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overhead item' suggests business costs, but it is something worn on the head.
explanation.definitionFit: A curl of hair hangs from the head, literally an item overhead.

clue.text: Descriptive of African flower, blue or white

definitions.text: Descriptive of African flower, blue or white

parts.words: Descriptive of African flower, blue or white
parts.note: a flower is something that flows, a river; Africa's great river has Blue and White branches

explanation.surface: A botanical term for an African bloom in blue or white.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' means one that flows: the Nile, whose two branches are the Blue and the White.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means relating to the Nile, Africa's longest river.

clue.text: Dance record follows arrangement of notes

indicators.note: follows places the record after the rearranged letters
an arrangement of the letters of notes puts them in a new order

parts.note: EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A dance record comes after a musical arrangement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrangement of' turns NOTES into ONEST, and 'follows' puts EP after it.
explanation.definitionFit: An early twentieth-century ballroom step in quick march time is a kind of dance.

clue.text: He may grow up a determined wooer

definitions.text: He may grow up a determined wooer

parts.words: He may grow up a determined wooer
parts.note: the nursery song 'A frog he would a-wooing go', and the young form that grows into that frog

explanation.surface: A boy who might mature into a persistent suitor.
explanation.walkthrough: The nursery song 'A frog he would a-wooing go' makes the frog a determined wooer; the young swimmer grows up into one.
explanation.definitionFit: The larva of a frog grows into the adult amphibian.

clue.text: Hide a little lower

definitions.meaning: leather from a young cow, as in calfskin
a young animal that lows, a small mooer

explanation.surface: Crouch down a bit to stay out of sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lower' is not 'more down' but 'one that lows' (moos); a little one is a young cow.
explanation.definitionFit: The skin of a young bovine is leather; the young of cattle is a small animal that moos.

clue.text: Constable — academician and nut when deprived of oils

parts.note: a constable is a police officer, a cop
RA is a Royal Academician

explanation.surface: The painter Constable was a Royal Academician and a nut.
explanation.walkthrough: Constable looks like the painter, who was an RA, but here it is a police officer.
explanation.definitionFit: The dried kernel of the coconut is the source pressed for coconut oil.

clue.text: Means of raising capital for an author

parts.note: a jack is a device for raising a car
the capital city of England

explanation.surface: Fundraising methods for a writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raising capital' reads as finance; it is a car jack plus England's capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: The American writer of The Call of the Wild is an author.

clue.text: VIP in eastern inn

definitions.meaning: a ruler or title of rank in Central Asia
a caravanserai, a resting place for travellers in the East

explanation.surface: An important person staying at an oriental hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: A Central Asian ruler is an important person; the same word is a caravanserai where travellers lodge.

clue.text: Little coughs taken. up by dressmakers

definitions.meaning: small throat-clearing sounds, as in 'hum and haw'
turned-up edges on garments that are taken up when shortened

explanation.surface: Seamstresses catch slight colds.
explanation.walkthrough: A dressmaker shortens a skirt by taking up its edge; the small coughs are throat-clearings.
explanation.definitionFit: Short throat-clearing noises; folded edges of cloth that dressmakers take up.

clue.text: Open admission of one who is under treatment

indicators.note: admission is letting something in, so the single letter is taken into the word for open

parts.note: patent means open and obvious
one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A frank confession by someone receiving medical care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admission of' puts I inside PATENT (obvious).
explanation.definitionFit: Someone receiving medical care is a doctor's case.

clue.text: An extra headlight?

parts.note: read as a light round the head, like a saint's halo in a painting, rather than a car lamp

explanation.surface: A spare lamp for the front of a car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Headlight' suggests a car, but it is a light around a head.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a halo, a ring of light round the head of a holy figure in art.

clue.text: Defective tyres can produce strain

indicators.note: defective means faulty, so the letters are put together wrongly

explanation.surface: Faulty tyres on a car can cause stress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Defective' scrambles TYRES and CAN; 'strain' is not stress but a line of descent.
explanation.definitionFit: A strain is a line of descent or breeding, a family lineage.

clue.text: Fellow in felt cap is deprived of hope

indicators.note: in means the abbreviation for fellow goes inside the cap

parts.note: a beret is a soft felt cap

explanation.surface: A man wearing a felt hat is in despair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts F inside BERET.
explanation.definitionFit: Being desolate and robbed of hope is the sense, as in someone bereaved and lost.
